clue.text: With reference to a professional position

blocks.note: taken as written
a pro is a professional
pos. is the standard abbreviation for position

explanation.surface: Someone writing a memo about a professional job opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos is a formal preposition meaning concerning or regarding something just mentioned.

clue.text: Circus artiste trained a cobra to tango!

indicators.note: an animal that is trained is put through new moves, so these letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
Tango is the NATO alphabet word for T

explanation.surface: A circus performer has taught a snake to dance the tango.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat is a performer of gymnastic feats, a classic act in the circus ring.

clue.text: Great barge capsized at aquatic event

indicators.note: to barge is to shove roughly, so these letters are jostled out of order
a boat that capsizes turns over, so in a down clue these letters are turned upside down

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A big river barge turned over during a boating event.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a series of boat races, a sporting event held on water.

clue.text: Whine about partner, get a beating

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps round the second

blocks.note: to pule is to whimper or whine
in bridge, South is the partner of North

explanation.surface: Complaining about your spouse might earn you a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the players sit as North, South, East and West, and each is partnered with the one opposite, so partner can be N, S, E or W.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is the rhythmic beating of the heart felt in the arteries.

clue.text: Green site could become a National Park

indicators.note: could become says these letters may turn into something else when rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An unspoilt plot of land might one day be designated a protected park.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti in Tanzania is a famous national park, an example of the category named.

clue.text: Read about corrupt ítec and made a response

indicators.note: something corrupt has been spoiled or altered, so these letters are scrambled
about means around, so the first word goes round the scrambled letters

blocks.note: taken as written
tec is slang for a detective; the accented first letter is a stray

explanation.surface: Someone reads about a crooked detective and answers back.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue prints 'ítec', but the wordplay needs only TEC, slang for a detective; the extra accented letter is a stray character.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to respond to something, so reacted means made a response.

clue.text: Due in Brighton

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following word, waiting to be found

blocks.note: letters two to six of the town name

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests something arriving at Brighton, the seaside town; the answer is inside its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A right is something you are due or entitled to, as in 'it is your due'.

clue.text: Presenter has secure work

blocks.note: to anchor something is to fix it securely
to man a post is to work at it

explanation.surface: A TV host has landed a steady job.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorman is the main host of a news broadcast who links the reports together.

clue.text: Clobber the voters

blocks.note: first meaning: clothing, how someone is dressed (clobber is British slang for clothes)
second meaning: the number of people who vote in an election

explanation.surface: An order to beat up the electorate.
explanation.walkthrough: Clobber looks like a verb meaning hit, but it is the British slang noun for clothes or gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnout is a person's outfit, and also the body of people who come out to vote.

clue.text: Active people accepting sons are lazy types

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the first word holds the second inside it

blocks.note: doers are people who get things done
s is the abbreviation for son, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Energetic parents who take their sons in turn out to be idle.
explanation.walkthrough: Doss is British slang for idling or sleeping rough, so a dosser is a layabout.
explanation.definitionFit: Dossers are idlers who avoid effort, so they are lazy types.

clue.text: Professional uniform

blocks.note: first meaning: a ... soldier is a full-time professional, not a reservist
second meaning: even and consistent throughout

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the outfit a professional wears; uniform is the adjective, not the clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular describes a full-time professional soldier and also anything even or steady in pattern.

clue.text: General skills needed for racing vehicles

blocks.note: GOC stands for General Officer Commanding
arts are skills, as in the arts of war

explanation.surface: General abilities are required to drive in a motor race.
explanation.definitionFit: Go-carts are small open motor vehicles raced on tracks, also spelt go-karts.

clue.text: Squash, ram and headbutt

blocks.note: a ram is a butter, something that butts
to nut someone is British slang for headbutting them

explanation.surface: A list of violent moves: squash, ram and headbutt.
explanation.walkthrough: Squash looks like a verb in a list of attacks, but it is the vegetable; ram is a noun too, the animal that butts.
explanation.definitionFit: Butternut is a variety of winter squash with pale orange flesh.

clue.text: Australia has ace sea air!

blocks.note: Oz is the nickname for Australia
an ace counts as one in cards

explanation.surface: A boast that Australia's seaside air is excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a popular term for fresh, bracing air at the seaside.

clue.text: Brown appears in panto as Tinkerbell

indicators.note: appears in says the letters show up inside the following words

blocks.note: spans the end of panto, all of as and the start of Tinkerbell

explanation.surface: An actor named Brown is cast as the fairy in a Christmas pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown looks like a surname; it is the cooking verb. A panto is a British Christmas pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: To toast bread is to brown it under heat, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Spinner makes changes to taunt Lara

indicators.note: making changes means altering, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket spin bowler tweaks things to needle the batsman Brian Lara.
explanation.walkthrough: Spinner suggests a spin bowler facing Lara, the West Indies batsman; here it is a creature that spins webs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarantula is a large hairy spider, and spiders spin silk.

clue.text: Reckons there are one million cars around

indicators.note: around says the following word goes round the earlier pieces

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
M is the abbreviation for million
estates are estate cars, what Americans call station wagons

explanation.surface: Someone guesses there are a million cars about.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to calculate roughly, so estimates and reckons are synonyms.

clue.text: Mean to stay to provide support for 1 down?

blocks.note: tight means stingy
a stay is a rope bracing a mast; to just leads in

explanation.surface: A miser stays put to hold up a circus performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 down is ACROBAT; the question mark flags that a tightrope is one kind of support an acrobat walks on.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightrope is a taut wire that bears a balancing circus performer, so it supports an acrobat.

clue.text: Nobody's inferior to Heather

blocks.note: under means below in rank
ling is common heather

explanation.surface: No one ranks below Heather.
explanation.walkthrough: Nobody's reads as 'nobody is', with Nobody the definition; Heather looks like a woman's name but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: An underling is a lowly subordinate, someone of no importance, a nobody.

clue.text: Skimpy garment's first to go in strip!

indicators.note: first to go says the opening letter is removed

blocks.note: a sundress is a light, bare-shouldered summer dress

explanation.surface: In a striptease, the flimsy item comes off first.
explanation.definitionFit: To undress is to take off your clothes, so it means strip.

clue.text: Method of giving eye medication to someone with ataxia?

blocks.note: first meaning: the small squeeze tube that releases liquid a bead at a time
second meaning, whimsical: one who lets things fall, as ataxia impairs coordination

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, whimsical meaning: ataxia is loss of muscle coordination, so its sufferer may let things fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A dropper is a pipette for eye drops, and literally anyone who lets things fall.

clue.text: Irritates the drug squad, according to informant

indicators.note: according to an informant means as an informer says it, so the sound is what counts

blocks.note: narcs is slang for narcotics officers

explanation.surface: A police informer reports that something is annoying the drug squad.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is apt: a nark is itself British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: To nark is British slang for to annoy, so narks means irritates.

clue.text: Obtain rhenium, aluminium, iodine and selenium

blocks.note: Re is the chemical symbol for rhenium
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium
I is the chemical symbol for iodine
Se is the chemical symbol for selenium

explanation.surface: A chemist's shopping list of four elements to get hold of.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise a sum is to obtain it from a sale, as in the house realised a good price.

clue.text: Courts obstruct national governing bodies

indicators.note: to obstruct is to stand around in the way, so the first word wraps round the second

blocks.note: to see someone is to date or court them
Nat is the abbreviation for national

explanation.surface: Law courts block national legislatures.
explanation.walkthrough: Courts suggests law courts, but here it is the verb for dating someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A senate is a legislative assembly, a body that governs a state or university.

clue.text: Run into drink and perish

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the first letter sits within the second word

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
to down a drink is to swallow it in one

explanation.surface: Someone falls into the water and dies.
explanation.definitionFit: To drown is to die by suffocating under water, a particular way to perish.

clue.text: In the company of tense introvert

definitions.note: noun in the clue, while the answer is an adjective; read as 'introverted'

blocks.note: with means accompanied by
drawn means strained or tense-looking

explanation.surface: A shy person looks strained among other people.
explanation.definitionFit: A withdrawn person is reserved and unsociable, the typical character of an introvert.

clue.text: Perhaps spelt "whet" without a vowel?

blocks.note: surface reading: a query about how a word is written, missing a vowel
setter's reading: spelt is a grain, an example of the answer, and removing a vowel from the answer leaves whet

explanation.walkthrough: Spelt looks like the past tense of spell, but it is an ancient grain; take the A out of the answer and you get whet.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelt is a primitive species of the cereal grain, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Question is the same but different

indicators.note: different means made unlike before, so these letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same
taken as written

explanation.surface: A paradox: is it the same yet different?
explanation.definitionFit: To doubt something is to question whether it is true.

clue.text: Finally take wife back

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: the final letter of take
a wife is a spouse

explanation.surface: A husband at last welcomes his wife home.
explanation.walkthrough: Back sits at the end, looking like part of take ... back; it is the definition, as in back a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to adopt and support it, so it means back.

clue.text: ICU lost amazing eye specialist

indicators.note: amazing suggests something astonishing has happened to these letters, leaving them jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written; ICU is an intensive care unit

explanation.surface: A hospital intensive care unit has lost a brilliant eye doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: An oculist is an old term for an ophthalmologist or optician, a doctor of eyes.

clue.text: 17 across raves about books

indicators.note: about means in a different arrangement, so these letters are moved around

blocks.note: taken as written
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A minion gets excited about reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 across is UNDERLING, so the definition is a cross-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: A servant is a subordinate who works for others, much like an underling.

clue.text: Dishes containing a couple of enchiladas and limes, perhaps

indicators.note: a couple means two, so only the first two letters of the next word are taken

blocks.note: the opening pair of letters of enchiladas
limes are trees (lindens), an example flagged by perhaps

explanation.surface: A menu of plates featuring enchiladas and lime.
explanation.walkthrough: Limes suggests the citrus fruit; here it is the lime tree, or linden.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrees are dishes of a meal, the main course in America or a course before the main one in Britain.
